Formulation:
The patient presents with several weeks to months of low mood, fatigue, anhedonia (decreased interest in activities), sleep disturbance, poor concentration, and reduced energy, temporally associated with a new job. Medical contributors (hypothyroidism on levothyroxine) and sleep disruption are relevant; psychosocial stressor (new employment) may contribute via an adjustment process. No current suicidality reported. Plan includes medical evaluation to exclude or address medical contributors, particularly thyroid function and anemia, and mental health assessment aimed at clarifying mood disorder status and treatment planning.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Return to previous level of functioning; regain energy and interest; restore sleep and routine
- Clinical Goal(s): Alleviate depressive symptoms; optimize medical contributors (thyroid function, potential anemia); improve sleep and daytime functioning
- Actions (Patient): Attend in-person GP exam; comply with prescribed or recommended blood tests; track symptoms and sleep; engage in consistent daily routine; communicate concerns
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Conduct comprehensive physical exam; order labs (TSH, Free T4, CBC with ferritin, metabolic panel); assess thyroid management (levothyroxine dosing/adequacy); screen for depression severity; discuss treatment options (psychotherapy, pharmacotherapy as indicated); arrange follow-up

Secondary Problem (Adjustment disorder with depressed mood related to new job):
- Patient Goal(s): Adapt to new work situation; maintain sleep and energy; engage in activities
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify work-related stressors; implement coping strategies and sleep hygiene; monitor mood response to work changes
- Actions (Patient): Implement sleep hygiene strategies; set reachable daily activity goals; discuss work-related stress with clinician; practice stress management techniques
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide psychoeducation on sleep and stress management; consider referral to CBT-I or psychotherapy if symptoms persist; monitor mood and functioning; coordinate with workplace accommodations if needed

Tertiary Problem (Hypothyroidism contributing to fatigue/mood symptoms):
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve euthyroid state and symptom improvement
- Clinical Goal(s): Obtain thyroid function testing; adjust thyroid therapy as indicated; monitor mood and energy
- Actions (Patient): Take medications as prescribed; attend labs; report any new symptoms
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Order and review TSH/Free T4 levels; assess adequacy of levothyroxine dosing; coordinate endocrinology referral if indicated; re-evaluate mood/depression symptoms after thyroid optimization

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: plan for medical evaluation (labs and in-person exam), differentiation of mood symptoms from medical causes, sleep hygiene, importance of follow-up, safety given current mood state (SI denial)
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Worsening depressed mood, anhedonia, increased sleep disturbance, persistent fatigue, thoughts of worthlessness or suicide, significant decrease in functioning
- Coping Strategies: Maintain regular sleep-wake schedule, establish routine, light physical activity as tolerated, stress management techniques, seek support from spouse/comfortable confidants, adhere to medical follow-up

- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Major depressive disorder (High) — Rationale: persistent low mood, fatigue, poor concentration, anhedonia, decreased energy, sleep disturbance, onset after a psychosocial stressor (new job); no current suicidality
- Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (Medium) — Rationale: symptoms cluster following notable life stressor (recent job change) within weeks to months
- Hypothyroidism (undertreated) (Medium) — Rationale: history of hypothyroidism; fatigue, cognitive slowing, mood changes could reflect thyroid dysfunction; no thyroid labs available yet to confirm status

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements: MSE details are incomplete; no laboratory results available in transcript; vital signs not provided; follow-up date not documented; detailed functional impairment not quantified
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted
- Transcript quality notes: Some portions of dialogue are concise or cut off; specific exam findings and some lab data are not recorded; mood/affect nuances not fully detailed

Notes:
- If a specific lab result becomes available (e.g., TSH, Free T4, CBC with ferritin), update the plan to reflect objective thyroid/autonomic/metabolic status.
- If depressive or anxiety symptoms persist or worsen despite medical optimization, consider escalation to psychotherapy (e.g., CBT) and/or pharmacotherapy per guideline-directed care.
